key_insight: Gradient-aware AI agents can autonomously propose, train, and revise turbulence closures using feedback from a differentiable CFD solver.
engineering_relevance: This framework could reduce manual closure-design effort while improving agreement with target flow statistics in turbulence simulations.
method: Pose discovery as a bilevel problem: LLM agents search closure forms, while gradient-based training tunes parameters.
Embed analytical, neural, or hybrid closures in a GPU-native differentiable CFD solver and validate the gradient path.
Use truncated-horizon gradients and simulation feedback to guide training and subsequent proposals.
evidence_signal: Demonstrations span 2D turbulence and 3D channel-flow LES; gradient-based training recovers reference coefficients not reached by forward evaluation alone within the same budget and improves agreement with targeted statistics.
watch_item: Truncated-horizon gradients enable training under chaotic dynamics, but performance beyond the demonstrated flows and target statistics remains unestablished.
paper_title: Gradient-Aware AI Agents for Autonomous Turbulence Model Discovery via Differentiable CFD
